To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insulin-mediated regulation of hepatic IGFBP- 1 gene expression is mTOR- and PI 3- kinase-dependent, and that H(2)(2) selectively antagonises mTOR-dependent insulin signalling.
the insulin-mediated inhibition of IGFBP gene expression and mTOR signalling is impaired by oxidative stresses, which may explain the development of insulin-resistance and type 2 diabetes.
insulin-induced activation of mTOR signalling and repression of hepatic IGFBP- 1 gene expression are antagonized by oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which insulin regulates hepatic gene expression, and how oxidative stress can interfere with these mechanisms.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the hepatic insulin-like factor-binding protein (IGFBP)-1 gene.
the mechanisms by which insulin regulates gene expression in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

insulin and oxidative stresses, such that are generated by the use of H2O2, do not have the same effects on IGFBP1 gene expression, and this may be related to the differential effects of these two factors on mTOR signalling.
H(2)(2)O(1) antagonizes insulin-induced mTOR-dependent signalling and IGFBP- 1 gene expression in hepatoma cells.
H(2)(2) selectively blocks the mTOR-dependent insulin-mediated repression of the IGFBP- 1 gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H(2)(2)O selectively inhibits mTOR-dependent insulin actions, and that this inhibition may contribute to the development of insulin-resistant diabetes.
H(2)(2)(2)O selectively antagonizes insulin-mediated repression of hepatic IGFBP- 1 gene expression by selectively blocking mTOR-dependent insulin signalling.
H(2)(O(2)) does not'm imic' but rather 'antagonize' insulin repression of IGFPB-1 expression in H4IE cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin resistance is a complex phenomenon that is not simply due to the 'oxidation' of insulin signalling.
insulin and oxidative stress have opposing actions on hepatic IGFBP- 1 gene expression, and that this effect is mediated by mTOR-dependent signalling.
H(2)(O(2)) does not mimic the action of insulin on IGFBP1 gene expression.
